positioning: The last five days of Christmas. Fifty more cats. One loud finish.
story: The count stands at 28. Fifty more cats are on their way.
Eight Ragdolls roll down the stairs on Sunday. Nine Persians pounce on Monday. Ten Munchkins march on Tuesday. Eleven Devons dash around the well on Wednesday.
On Thursday, New Year’s Eve, twelve Abys arch on the well and the courtyard is complete. That makes 78 cats, the exact sum of the song.
Friday is New Year’s Day. Saturday is for the cat who was not on the list.
Write down what went well this year. Write down what made you laugh. A cat would tell you the same thing. The best gifts are the ones you can sit in.
Then close the old year. The new one begins with a Norwegian Forest Cat.
rank_cap: cats in all, by New Year’s Eve
fblocks: Tradition runs the twelve days from Christmas Day to January 5. We count to New Year’s Eve, then keep going.
Ragdoll, the cat that goes limp and happy. Persian, the long-haired classic. Devon Rex, the pixie.
Fireworks frighten many cats. Keep them inside, close the windows and give them a quiet room on New Year’s Eve.
Nap more. Knock fewer things off the shelf. Never miss a sunbeam.
50 cats this week. 78 in all. 50 breed weeks ahead.
days: Eight Ragdolls slide down the steps in a limp heap. Not one of them minds.
Persians are among the oldest recognized breeds, with a long coat and a flat face. Nine of them pounce on the ribbon anyway.
Munchkins have short legs from a natural gene and move just fine. Ten march across the courtyard in a line.
Devon Rex have wide ears, big eyes and a coat of soft down, and they act like pixies. Eleven Devons dash around the well.
The year ends with twelve Abys arching on the well. Stretch before you start. Start small. Be loud.
New Year’s Day belongs to the first walk. Where will yours go?
Every list leaves someone out. The rescue cat gets the warmest bed.
last_walk:
The old year goes out the gate.
A rescue cat sleeps in the warmest bed and the stockings are all full. Seventy-eight cats are quiet at last. Tomorrow the calendar turns, and a Norwegian Forest Cat walks out of the snow.
